title: Granularity from bounded spectral sparsity
statement: Let $S\ge 2$ be an integer and let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional cube over $ bf_2$ to signs. If the number of nonzero vector Fourier coefficients of the real-valued function $x\mapsto f(x)$ is at most $S$, then this function is vector Fourier granular with granularity $2^{1-\lfloor\log_2 S\rfloor}$; that is, each Fourier coefficient on the sign cube is an integer multiple of this number.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a natural number with $2\le S$
$f$ maps the $n$-dimensional $ bf_2$ cube to signs
The spectral sparsity of $x\mapsto \operatorname{signValue}(f(x))$ is at most $S$
